# /crav1-tighten-spec

lane: specify | group: Specify | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.0.0 | prompts: 1
purpose: Walk an existing spec issue-by-issue.
use_when: The spec is still mushy
reads: Reads `spec.md`, diagrams, ADRs, reviewer findings already in the chat, and, when the slice is partial or `## In the code` names paths, the committed code on the repo and branch that spec names.
writes: Writes only the picked issue in `spec.md` and, when that pick says so, the named diagram, ADR, or export. Writes a branch onto the spec only after a yes. A stale research mark may be one issue. It does not clear the mark and it does not rewrite the research note.
leaves alone: Leaves application code and unpicked issues alone. A spec with no code behind it skips that read.
limits: a different open repo or branch, a missing branch, a stub, or a spec too thin for that read stops and does not tighten. `suggest` does not patch. A disagreement with the code is called out and the spec is not rewritten to match the code. Finish, add a test, and leave are not choices here. A quoted note in `docs/notes/` gets its slug in `used_by` and a `Full source:` link; notes are never absorbed.
flow:
- the batch hint names the item, for example `Login page (I1) keep`.
- When the slice is partial or `## In the code` names paths, reads the committed code on the repo and branch the spec names before wording issues.
- more than 8 issues starts with one line of counts (issues to fix, open questions, small wording) and does not print the full list.
- Each time, one issue or a small group; one by one is always offered.
- An issue whose only work is an Answered line, or that repeats an open question, is one line passed to `/crav1-resolve-open-questions`, with no menu.
- eight or fewer issues are one card.
- `yes (Recommended)` applies every recommendation.
- Typed changes go on that card's free-text answer, for example `I1 B, I3 keep`.
- that card is asked only after a findings table in the same reply (Id, Issue, Options, Recommendation).
- The card names each item, for example `I1 acceptance is not yes/no: A make-testable`.
- It does not say `table above`.
- The command is `<interpreter> -X utf8 <skill crav1-tighten-plan>/scripts/batch_offer.py --title "Tighten-plan batch" --items <file>`.
- It prints no card without rows.
- reads every listed work branch without checkout; a yes on writing the branch adds to the `Branch:` list; a listed branch that is gone and not merged is offered `(dropped)` (`mark-dropped`); a deleted branch whose work is in the base shows `merged, branch deleted`.
- reads and writes the `(spec branch)` and `(into …)` markers on the Match `Branch:` list after a yes.
- a yes on writing the branch adds one Match `Branch:` line in sorted place (repo, then branch); never `; `-joined.
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Calls no skill.
you run next: /crav1-resolve-open-questions; /crav1-finalize-commit
first: `/crav1-tighten-spec @docs/specs/<slug>/spec.md`
walkthrough: from-draft-spec.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.207.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-tighten-spec.md
